q: I have a 60-second ad; the client wants 30, 15 and 6-second versions.
a: 1. Duplicate the sequence for each length (`edit.duplicate`) so the 60 stays intact; name them with the length. 2. Cut each down to the core message, keeping the brand and call to action at the end. 3. Fit the music to each length with Remix (`clip.remix.enable`, Remix Properties) so it still ends properly. 4. Queue all four exports (`export.queue.add`, `export.queue.start`).

q: 6 second bumper from a long spot, what do I keep
a: One idea: the strongest shot or moment, the product, the logo; titles big and short. Duplicate the sequence first and cut there, music fitted with Remix or a short sting.

q: Keep the end card identical across all cutdowns.
a: Make the end card a source graphic (`graphics.upgradeToSourceGraphic`) or a template, so changing it once updates every version.

q: Replace the messy room behind me with a nicer background, no green screen.
a: Revolution can't cut a person out automatically. Options: a hand-drawn mask around you on Opacity (`masks.add`), feathered and tracked or keyframed as you move, over a new background on the track below; or blur and darken the real background instead (a blurred copy with an inverted mask), which hides the mess with much less work. Next time a plain wall or a green screen makes it easy.

q: background replacement but my hair edges look terrible
a: Hand masks can't follow hair: feather more and keep the new background similar in brightness to the old one so the edge blends; a blurred background hides edges better than a sharp replacement.

q: Darken and desaturate the background behind me instead of replacing it.
a: On a node, an ellipse window around you, Inverted, soft (`grade.window.0.invert`), with Gain and Saturation down outside, tracked if you move (`masks.track`).

q: Passport-stamp style graphics popping onto the screen for each city.
a: A stamp graphic per city (an image with transparency or shape + text layers) that pops in: Scale keyframes from about 130 % down to 100 % in a few frames with a slight Rotation, Opacity up, eased; a stamp thud sound. Save it as a template with the city name editable.

q: stamps should look inked and a bit rough
a: Multiply blend on the stamp (paper shows through), Roughen Edges for a rough edge, and a slight Opacity below 100 %.

q: Animated dotted travel route plus stamps on a map image.
a: A map image as background with slow Scale moves; the route as short line shapes appearing one after another (keyframed Opacity or Scale), stamps popping in at each stop.

q: I need to swap the song in my edit but keep it in rhythm.
a: Place the new song, then re-time: markers on the new song's beats (M while playing), and slide or trim edits to the nearest markers with Snap on (`sequence.snap`). Remix fits the new song to the edit's length (`clip.remix.enable`). Cuts that land on phrases matter more than every beat.

q: new song has a different tempo, cuts feel off
a: Re-cut to the new phrases rather than forcing the old cuts; roll edits a few frames at a time (`tool.rolling`) to sit on accents.

q: Copyright claim on my music, replace it with a licensed track.
a: Use music whose licence covers the platform and keep the licence file; replace the track, re-time a few edits to the new beats, and set loudness again (about −14 LUFS for YouTube).

q: How do I cut a dialogue scene shot with a wide, two mediums and close-ups?
a: Start wide to set the space, move into mediums as the conversation settles, and save close-ups for the important lines; cut on action and on reactions, J / L cuts for flow. String out the takes first so you know the best performances, then build the scene in passes.

q: continuity errors between takes, cup in different hand
a: Cut away to a reaction or a close-up when the mismatch would show, or cut on a moment of movement so the eye follows the action instead.

q: Pick the best take of each line quickly.
a: Mark selects in the Source monitor (markers, subclips), compare takes back to back, and use three-point edits to place the chosen ones.

q: Rocky-style training montage with energy that builds.
a: Short clips cut to a driving song (markers on beats, Snap), getting shorter and faster towards the climax; a few speed ramps (stepped) and slow-motion hero moments; split screens for side-by-side progress (Motion Position or a mask); end on the big moment with a hit.

q: montage feels repetitive
a: Vary shot sizes and angles, alternate fast and slow, insert a breather moment, and cut on phrases and accents rather than every beat.

q: Show days passing in the montage.
a: A small text graphic 'Day 1', 'Day 30' from a template, or a quick dissolve chain with the light changing; cooler early, warmer later in the grade.

q: Export just the audio of my video as a podcast file.
a: Export with an audio format (WAV for a master, AAC / M4A for distribution) from the Export page, or use an audio preset; check loudness first (about −16 LUFS for podcasts, peaks under −1 dBTP). Extract Audio (`clip.extractAudio`) writes a single clip's sound to its own file instead.

q: separate files for dialogue, music and effects (stems)
a: Keep dialogue, music and effects on their own tracks or submixes, then export with only one solo'd at a time (mute the others), or hand off with an interchange file for the sound mixer.

q: Mono podcast file from a stereo edit.
a: Map the channels to mono (Modify ▸ Audio Channels, `clip.audioChannels`) or choose mono in the audio export settings; check nothing was panned hard to one side.

q: Wedding speech recorded on the venue mic: hum, quiet speaker, loud laughter.
a: 1. DeHum at the mains frequency (Essential Sound ▸ Repair) for the hum. 2. Dynamics to even out the quiet speaker and the loud laughter; clip gain (`clip.audioGain`) to bring the voice up. 3. Reduce Noise lightly. 4. A limiter on the Mix for the laughter peaks.

q: the speaker moves away from the mic and gets quiet
a: Raise those passages with Volume keyframes or clip gain on split pieces, then Dynamics to smooth; Voice Isolation can lift a distant voice out of room noise.

q: Cut the speech shorter without it sounding cut.
a: Cut between sentences (use the transcript to find them), put short audio crossfades on each edit, and cover visible jumps with guest reaction shots.

q: Turn hours of dashcam footage into a short clip of the near-miss.
a: Find the moment (markers while scrubbing), cut a short piece around it, slow the key second (Speed / Duration, stepped), stabilise if shaky (Warp Stabilizer), and punch in on the action (Motion Scale); a freeze frame with a circle shape on the other car explains it.

q: blur number plates in dashcam video
a: A tracked Mosaic or blur on each plate (`tracking.blurRegion`); fast-moving plates may need the track fixed by hand.

q: Dashcam timestamp is burned in and distracting.
a: Crop it out by scaling up a little (Motion Scale) or cover it with a blurred patch (a masked blur); you can't remove burned-in text cleanly.

q: Highlight the mouse cursor in my screen recording.
a: There's no automatic cursor highlight. A small yellow ellipse shape in a graphic on V2, placed on the cursor and attached with Attach to Track (`tracking.attach`, Position only); clicks can get a quick Scale pulse. Flat screen areas may lose the track: fix by hand.

q: zoom follows the cursor around the screen
a: Keyframe Motion Position and Scale on the recording to follow the cursor's area, eased; or track the cursor and copy its movement into the zoom by hand.

q: Click sound and ripple at each click.
a: Markers at each click (`markers.add`), a click sound on an SFX track and a small circle shape scaling up and fading at each marker (a preset makes it quick).
